9d58501f2df38d8e: BANGKOK: Thailand's cabinet on Sunday approved special holidays on Sept 28 and 29 for civil servants in Bangkok and three surrounding provinces due to heavy rainfall.

"The measure aims to reduce travel and ease traffic disruptions for the public," the government said, adding that important official business scheduled during the holidays may continue as deemed appropriate by their heads.

The holiday decision could have interfered with the reading by Thailand's Constitutional Court of a verdict in a case brought by the country's official ombudsman, relating to ballots used in the February election, which could put the election results in doubt. However, the court said the reading would go ahead as planned on Monday.

The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration declared the capital a disaster-affected area on Saturday after nearly 300mm of rain fell over 48 hours, leading to flooding on major roads that left some cars partly submerged.
Floodwater receded on Sunday as rainfall eased, but some residents remained stranded in their homes.--REUTERS
b57a0075a41fc3e8: NAGOYA: Puripol Boonson broke new ground for Thailand athletics on Sunday, storming to the 200 metres gold on a damp track to complete the Asian Games sprint double while China's javelin sensation Yan Ziyi defeated an Olympic champion.
Having claimed the 100m gold in 9.90 seconds two days ago, 20-year-old Puripol became the first Thai sprinter to break the 20-second barrier in the 200m with a run of 19.88.

His time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium matched the seven-year-old Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye and confirmed him as one of the continent's most exciting track talents ahead of next year's world championships in Beijing.

"I'm going to aim for more golds and more records. I can't say how fast it's going to be, but it's going to be more records and faster," said Puripol, who was more than a half-second quicker than China's runner-up Huang Youwen.
Puripol was one of several young guns firing at the track and field.

Yan, 18, who has taken the athletics world by storm in her debut season this year, needed only one throw of 70.46 to beat Olympic champion and home hero Haruka Kitaguchi (62.70) for her first Asian Games gold.
One of athletics' biggest drawcards was lost when former Olympic champion Mutaz Barshim pulled out of the high jump due to injury, leaving Taiwan's Fu Chao-hsuan to take the title (2.25m).

Bahrain's Olympic champion Winfred Yavi cruised to the 3,000m steeplechase title in 9:04.36, adding to her 10,000m gold, while Singapore's Shanti Pereira retained the women's 200m title in 22.78, becoming the first to win the event back-to-back.
Beaten by China's rising star Chen Yujie for the 100m gold, Pereira denied the 17-year-old by 0.15 seconds in the 200m.
"I was like, 'No, you (Chen) got it that day. Today is me. Nothing in the world is going (to) stop me'," said the 30-year-old.
CRAMPED ATHLETES

Five years after Japan staged an Olympics without fans due to COVID-19 restrictions, the Aichi-Nagoya Games have been under scrutiny over a lack of fan interest, and rainy weather proved a dampener on the eighth full day, with banks of empty seats at competition venues.

Accommodation has also been in the spotlight, with organisers opting to house athletes and officials in a mix of hotels, temporary wooden huts and a cruise ship. Some athletes had found them "rather cramped", an official admitted.

South Korea beat hosts Japan 3-1 in a battle of Asia's baseball powers for the men's gold, while squash powerhouse Malaysia celebrated as Ng Eain Yow and Sivasangari Subramaniam won back-to-back gold in the men's and women's singles respectively.
The Malaysian duo became the first athletes to earn quota berths to the sport's Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028.
Subramaniam, who has gone from strength to strength since a near-fatal crash in 2022, said: "World number one and an Olympic gold medal is my goal."

Sunday kicked off with penalty-laden race walk events, with India's Priyanka Goswami, a Commonwealth Games runner-up, disqualified for racking up too many red cards in the women's marathon, which was won by Kazakh Yasmina Toxanbayeva.
World bronze medallist Hayato Katsuki walked "cautiously" to win the men's marathon gold for Japan in 3:03:36, leaving a three-minute gap to China's runner-up Zhou Yingcheng.
"I'm confident that in terms of power, I'm the best in the world," said the 35-year-old, who won his second Games title after the 50-km gold at Jakarta 2018. --REUTERS

559590d1477de524: FAIRFORD: British counter-terrorism police were Sunday probing "a major" incident near a base used by the US air force after arresting five men on suspicion of "preparing a terrorist act", police said.

Armed officers detained the group in the early hours after a call to emergency services about three "suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base", London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement.
The suspects were initially held near the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford air base in Gloucestershire, southwest England, on suspicion of explosives offences.
Some 85 households in the nearby village of Whelford were advised to evacuate and army bomb disposal experts called in to examine three vans stopped on a rural road.
"Counter Terrorism Policing can now confirm they are leading an investigation into an incident which took place overnight near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire," the Met statement added.
Broadcast aerial footage showed a bomb disposal robot on a rural road moving around the vans, two of which had their rear doors open.
Police believed the incident had been "contained" and a 400 metre cordon had been put in place.
Armed officers could be seen guarding the entrance to the base.
In March, then prime minister Keir Starmer granted permission for "defensive" US action against Iranian missile sites from two UK bases including Fairford.
New Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being kept updated on the incident, a government spokesperson said.
"We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe," the spokesperson said.
"It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing."
Defence Minister Wes Streeting thanked "emergency and specialist teams" deployed to the scene.
"We can be reassured that this is being dealt with," he said on X.
Gloucestershire Police said earlier it had declared a "major incident" with several men arrested "on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act."
- VILLAGERS EVACUATED -
Residents were evacuated to a nearby leisure centre, police said.
Villager Julian Tudsbery said he was woken and advised to leave at about 7am (0600 GMT) by police "banging on the door."
He said a fellow villager had alerted police in the middle of the night after spotting the vans.
"They phoned the airbase police, who didn't answer the phone. It just rang out so she dialled 999," he told the BBC.
Fairford is the UK base of the 501st Combat Support Wing, a US air force administrative support wing, which said in a statement that no US air force personnel had been involved in the incident.
"The 501st Combat Support Wing appreciates the swift response and continued support of our local law enforcement partners," it said.
"We remain in close coordination with our UK partners to help ensure the safety and security of both our military and local communities," it added.
The MP for the area, Roz Savage, described the situation as "worrying."
"I have contacted the police for further updates and I've been told that it is believed the incident is contained," she said on X.
The incident comes amid concerns about the actions of hostile foreign states.
Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood has accused Iran and Russia of using proxies to carry out criminal activities on their behalf on UK territory.
Earlier this month, reports said British military sites had been targeted by drones more than 300 times over the past year.

Britain's defence ministry did not disclose who was behind the drone activity, but the figures come as European countries have warned of an increase in suspected Russian hybrid operations on their territory.--AFP

233c0d448d84ec22: NAGOYA: India captain Shreyas Iyer ruled out any complacency ahead of Monday's Asian Games quarter-finals against Afghanistan, conceding last week's scare against Japan had jolted the Twenty20 world champions out of any complacence.

In a rain-hit match at Sano, India edged Japan in a five-over shootout to lift the Suzuki Cup in the maiden one-off meeting between the men's sides — a jolt that underlined the danger of underestimating any opponent in alien conditions.
India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are seeded directly into the last eight, while Nepal, Afghanistan, Malaysia and Hong Kong advanced from the preliminary groups.
With India's women having successfully defended their Asian Games title, attention now turns to Iyer's side to emulate them.
"Not just Afghanistan, no team can be taken lightly at any stage - just look at how tough Japan made it for us the other day," Iyer said on Sunday.
"The pitches here cannot be set to a certain standard, so to adapt is key. It will be challenging for all the teams."
Expectation remains sky-high for the sport's most followed team, and Iyer acknowledged the scrutiny that comes with the jersey.
"Whenever you represent India, there are a lot of expectations, that you have to finish at the top. That is always there," Iyer said of the "good pressure."

"We have to be mentally prepared irrespective of whatever the situation is going to be. We did get a decent chance to warm up and knock the ball around today, and now the task is to adapt quickly to the pitch," he said.

f708a7d824b9d1ef: NAGOYA: Qatar's former world champion and Olympic gold medallist Mutaz Barshim has withdrawn from the men's high jump final at the Asian Games, the Qatar Athletics Federation said on X on Sunday, without providing further details.

832c71bf99a4c966: NAGOYA: China's 18-year-old Yan Ziyi showcased her rare talent by shattering the Asian Games record to win the javelin, as a medallist failed a doping test and a decorated badminton player branded the event in Japan "sad."
Golds were up for grabs on day eight in sports including athletics, diving, skateboarding, squash and weightlifting.
On another wet day in Aichi-Nagoya, the teenager Yan demolished the opposition in the women's javelin with her first and only throw of the night of 70.46m.
It was a new Games record, smashing the 66.09m by compatriot Liu Shiying in 2018, and left Japan's reigning Olympic champion Haruka Kitaguchi in a distant second for silver (62.70m).
Yan's incredible throw was the sixth best of all time. The world record is 72.28m by Barbora Spotakova in 2008.
But Yan is closing in – she hurled 71.74m in May, the second best of all time.
On the track, Thailand's Puripol Boonson made it a sprint double, winning the men's 200m to go with his 100m crown.
His scintillating 19.88sec equalled the Asian record.
Asked how much faster he can run, the 20-year-old said: "I can't say how fast it's going to be, but it's going to be more records and faster."
- Eyes on LA -
Towards the end of day eight, China topped the medals table with 119 golds, with Japan second on 37 and South Korea on 20.
North Korea enjoyed more record-setting success in weightlifting, taking their overall haul in the sport to six golds out of an available 10 so far.
China maintained their unbeaten start in diving, while a pair of teenagers took gold in the street skateboarding finals.
China's Zhu Yuanling, 15, won the women's event and the 17-year-old Juni Kang of South Korea took the men's title.
Kang now has his eyes on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
"I want to be No.1 in LA," he said.
Malaysia reigned in the squash, with Ng Eain Yow winning the men's crown and compatriot Sivasangari Subramaniam prevailing in the women's singles.
Both booked spots to Los Angeles in the process.
- 'It was sad' -
Organisers in Aichi-Nagoya did not build a traditional athletes' village in a bid to save money, with competitors instead staying in hotels or temporary wooden units, and on a cruise ship.
India's multiple badminton medallist H.S. Prannoy said that made for a disappointing experience.
"It was sad," the 34-year-old, who won team bronze, said in a YouTube video published by the Badminton Association of India.
"It never felt like we were playing in an Asian Games, to be honest."
There have been a series of problems at the Games, including a shortage of rooms, long delays at the airport and poor transport services.
Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Shavkatov became the first medallist at the Games to test positive for doping.
Shavkatov, who won bronze in mixed martial arts, has been provisionally suspended after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, the International Testing Agency said.
The drug is a prescription heart medication that can improve endurance and accelerates muscle recovery. --AFP

ab98e282fa136e06: KUALA LUMPUR: China surpassed the 200-medal mark at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today, while Malaysia reached their pre-Games target of six gold medals on Day 8.
China reached 118 gold, 48 silver, and 38 bronze medals for a 204-medal haul.
Their 118 golds exceed the combined total of the next four nations: hosts Japan (37), South Korea (20), Uzbekistan (10), and Kazakhstan (9), who have 76 golds combined.
The result also secured China's 10th consecutive Asian Games with 100 or more gold medals, a streak dating back to Beijing 1990.
Japan are second with 37 gold, 60 silver, and 57 bronze (154 overall), with South Korea in third (20-23-39) ahead of Uzbekistan (10-17-11) and Kazakhstan (9-10-21).
Malaysia moved into 10th place with 16 medals (six gold, two silver, eight bronze), hitting its pre-Games target of six golds with a week of competition remaining.
The sixth gold was won on the squash court by world No. 5 S. Sivasangari, who beat India's Anahat Singh 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 in the women's final.
Earlier, defending champion Ng Eain Yow won the fifth gold by beating India's Abhay Singh 11-9, 11-5, 11-5.
Their victories added to earlier golds won by karatekas Adeola Fay Robert and Shahmalarani Chandran, eSports star Taj Izrin Aiman Taj Madira, and the men's sepak takraw team regu.
Diving added a silver through Enrique Maccartney Harold-Elvis Priestly Clement, and a bronze through Ong Ker Ying-Lee Yiat Qing.
Within Southeast Asia, Thailand lead in sixth overall on 9-7-10, with Malaysia second among Asean contingents in 10th.
Indonesia is 14th with two gold, five silver, and 17 bronze medals, followed by Singapore in 15th (2-5-3) and the Philippines in 16th (2-2-8).

32849a785e9efb54: ASTANA: The Higher Education Ministry began reviewing and restructuring public university holding companies last year, including UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd.

Its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, said the move was taken to ensure university holding companies could function more effectively and contribute to their respective institutions, particularly after the government stopped fully funding universities' financial needs in 2017.
"We have asked for all university holdings to be reviewed. Since last year, I have asked that we look at how to restructure the existing holding companies at universities.

"What we found was that some holdings were not functioning very well. That was the first step we took, and we have already begun several rounds of reviews to reassess these holdings, including UiTM Holdings," he said.
He said during his official visit to Kazakhstan for the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026 (MAHEF2026).

He was asked about his ministry's actions after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday called for a review of UiTM Holdings' management and governance following losses incurred by the company.
Zambry said some university holding companies had recorded profits while others had incurred losses, as such the business models of better-performing companies could serve as examples for others.
On UiTM, he said that a team had been established to comprehensively review efforts to strengthen the university, including aspects related to its holding company.
He said the team included Dr Nungsari Ahmad Radhi, Datuk Dr Hamzah Kassim, UiTM Board of Directors chairman Tan Sri Mohd Khamil Jamil and former higher education minister Tan Sri Idris Jusoh.
"We have set up a new team to look comprehensively at how we can reassess UiTM, and this also involves its holdings and so on.
"UiTM is a very important Bumiputera higher education institution that we need to safeguard and uphold to ensure that that no negative elements take root within it," he said.
Zambry said measures announced by Anwar yesterday aligned with efforts already undertaken by his ministry, adding that the ministry would continue with the review.
UiTM Holdings was previously reported to have recorded cumulative pre-tax losses of approximately RM157 million for the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 financial years.

400429558cbcc353: BAKU: George Russell closed the gap to championship-leading Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli at the top of the Formula One standings after fending off Red Bull's Max Verstappen to complete a lights-to-flag win in ‌Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the Italian fifth.

Russell took the flag just 0.196 seconds ahead of the flying Dutchman, who had started eighth but crossed the line nearly side-by-side with his Mercedes rival, after two safety car phases turned a Saturday cruise into a fight for survival for the Briton.
Frenchman Isack Hadjar completed a double podium for Red Bull, repaying the team's decision to give him a contract extension with third on his return to racing action.
"It's amazing to be back on the top step of the podium," said Russell, after closing the gap to Antonelli from 81 to 66 points in the overall standings with ⁠15 races completed.
"Every race since the (summer) break I have gone from strength to strength and I feel more like myself again."
RUSSELL'S FIRST WIN SINCE JUNE
Antonelli had started 16th after a rare error saw him crash out of Friday's qualifying.
His drive on Saturday was less like his Monza charge – where he went from 19th to first – and more a slow-burn recovery.
Saturday's win was the eighth of Russell's career, his third of the season and first since the Austrian Grand Prix in June.

It capped a dominant weekend for the Briton and had seemed a mere formality, with the 28-year-old leading off the line and opening up a comfortable lead ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Verstappen and Hadjar.
But all that changed on the 31st of the race's 51 laps when a crash for Williams racer Alex Albon brought out the safety car.
Russell's 11-second lead evaporated as the safety car bunched up the field.
Verstappen snatched second from Piastri into the first corner as the action resumed, with Russell unchallenged.

But the race was neutralised almost ‌instantly by ⁠another safety car when Argentine Franco Colapinto locked up and ploughed into Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, who in turn collected McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris.
The collision sidelined both Gasly and Norris on the spot, with the fuming Briton calling for the 23-year-old Colapinto to be banned.

Colapinto initially continued before pulling into the pits to retire. He was given a 10-second time penalty but the Argentine will have to serve it in the form of a five-place grid penalty at the next race in Malaysia as he failed to finish.
Russell had Verstappen right on his tail at the second restart.
The Mercedes driver kept the lead but was unable to shake off the chasing Red Bull, with the pair trading fastest laps.
It looked like the Dutchman, brushing the barriers as he ⁠hunted down his first win of the season, might just snatch victory on the final dash to the line but the Briton doggedly clung on.
"We had a good race, a tricky first stint on the mediums (tyres) but we got a good restart," said Verstappen.
"Then the final lap George lost boost and I got close, but it was not enough."
Behind them, Hadjar inherited third when ⁠Piastri locked up and took to the run-off area.
The Australian, who had started third, dropped to 14th compounding a miserable day for McLaren.
"It has been a very long six weeks since I injured myself," said Hadjar, who missed the last three races with a wrist injury.
"It was the right time to come back, I felt strong, I ⁠took it step by step to gain the confidence," added the 21-year-old who was also on the podium in Monaco.
Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari. His seven-times world champion teammate Lewis Hamilton was sixth.
Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad, who made contact with teammate Liam Lawson and sent the New Zealander into a spin, was seventh.
Esteban Ocon took eighth ahead of teammate Oliver Bearman in a double points finish for Haas. Carlos Sainz rounded out the top 10 for Williams. --REUTERS

4eca944c2bcb30ec: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam has formally taken over as president of Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS).
He was elected unopposed at the PBS 41st Annual Delegates Congress here yesterday, succeeding Datuk Seri Dr Maximus Johnity Ongkili.
Dr Joachim is the third president of the party after its founding president, Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan and Ongkili.
He will serve as president until 2029.

When nominations closed in August, Dr Joachim was the sole candidate for the presidency. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/08/1505710/dr-joachim-takes-pbs-presidency-joniston-elected-deputy-unopposed)

In his maiden policy speech as president, he said PBS could not allow its more than four decades of history to trap it in old approaches, but must continue renewing itself to remain relevant to present and future generations.

He said unity, stability and integrity would form the three main pillars of his leadership, with the party set to strengthen its organisational structure, embrace technology and digitalisation, and develop a new generation of leaders, particularly to engage younger Sabahans.
Dr Joachim also proposed a special task force comprising experienced party members to examine strategies and measures to strengthen and rejuvenate the party.

He said PBS would strengthen its policy and research capabilities and develop solutions to issues including the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), economy, education, employment, cost of living, rural development and technology.

36fa1862bd8877e2: KUALA LUMPUR: National squash players Ng Eain Yow and S. Sivasangari have made history as the sport's first qualifiers for the Olympic Games after winning two gold medals at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.

The achievement was highlighted on social media by the official Olympic Games account (@olympics), which acknowledged the pair as the first squash players to secure Olympic qualification places ahead of the sport's debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
"Malaysia make history!" the official @olympics page announced to its millions of followers.

"Eain Yow and Sivasangari confirm their Olympic places for Malaysia at #LA28 with victory in the men's and women's singles, respectively, at the #AsianGames. They become the first-ever squash players to secure Olympic places."

While former players, including eight-time world champion Datuk Nicol David, spent their careers unable to compete in the Olympics, Eain Yow and Sivasangari became the first names listed on the official qualification roster.
The Malaysians secured their gold medals at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena, winning both the men's and women's singles finals in straight games.
Sivasangari, the women's world No. 5, defeated India's Anahat Singh 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 to defend her Asian Games singles title.
Eain Yow, the men's world No. 17, retained his men's singles title by defeating India's Abhay Singh 11-9, 11-5, 11-5.

The International Olympic Committee said the athletes' spots remain subject to formal selection by the Olympic Council of Malaysia in accordance with the Olympic Charter and World Squash Federation criteria.

24da0d64b41b8754: ASTANA: Malaysia and Kazakhstan are looking to revive the momentum of higher education cooperation affected by the Covid-19 pandemic.

Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the the focus would now be expanded to strategic areas including artificial intelligence, nuclear energy, critical minerals and agriculture.

"Now is the best time for us to reconnect or rebuild what we have arranged together with Kazakhstan.
"At the same time, we have thousands of Kazakhstani students who previously studied in Malaysia and are now in various sectors, agencies and ministries.

The visit was held in conjunction with the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026 (MAHEF2026) organised by Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) to strengthen regional cooperation and student mobility.

Zambry said this development opens up opportunities for Malaysia to expand its higher education network across Central Asia, building on the growing ties following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to the region in 2024.
He said among the significant developments is the inaugural ministerial-level meeting on higher education involving Malaysia and Central Asian countries, with Kazakhstan hosting the first edition.
He said both parties have agreed in principle for the meeting to be made an annual event hosted in rotation, with Malaysia expected to host it next year.

He said Malaysia and Kazakhstan have also identified several areas for joint studies and research, including AI, nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, critical minerals and rare earth elements (REE), as well as agriculture.

The cooperation also includes dual-degree programmes to enable students from both countries to study at selected universities in Malaysia and Kazakhstan, apart from mobility programmes, industrial training and experience sharing.

Meanwhile, Zambry said EMGS plays a vital role in advancing the nation's higher education internationalisation agenda, with its approach to managing international students becoming a reference for several countries.

He said among EMGS' initiatives is the International Student Arrival Centre (ISAC), established in collaboration with the Malaysian Immigration Department and Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) as a one-stop centre to facilitate international students' affairs upon arrival in Malaysia.

Malaysia currently has about 170,000 international students from nearly 180 countries and is ranked 14th as an international education destination, with the country aiming to be in the world's top 10 in the future.

f5b02d759d10a99e: KUALA LUMPUR: China's 52-year streak of winning a medal in the Asian Games men's singles badminton event came to an end in Ichinomiya City after their shuttlers failed to reach the podium.

6332e926bb300704: LONDON: Former Stoke manager Tony Pulis said he feels "cheated" by his club's FA Cup final defeat against Manchester City.
Pulis was in charge of Stoke when they were beaten 1-0 by City at Wembley in the 2011 FA Cup showpiece.
It was a painful loss for Pulis, who was hoping to lead unfashionable Stoke to their first major trophy since the 1972 League Cup.
City's victory was their first significant success under their Abu Dhabi-based owners, setting the stage for over a decade of dominance.

However, City's achievements have been cast into doubt after they were reportedly found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League for breaching financial rules.
News of the decision, reached by an independent commission, was widely reported on Friday but no official announcement has been made by the Premier League.
City have strenuously denied the charges and their chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak on Saturday said he is still confident of proving the club's innocence.
City are expected to appeal against their eventual punishment, which is yet to be announced and could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.
There have also been calls for City to be stripped of the Premier League titles won since their 2008 takeover by Sheikh Mansour' Abu Dhabi United Group.
In a BBC Sport column on Sunday, Pulis said Stoke fans had been asking him: "When do we get our FA Cup?"

"I thought exactly the same. While the process is far from over because Manchester City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth," he said.
"I don't expect Manchester City to phone me or the club up and offer back the 2011 FA Cup and the winners' medals their players received.
"I don't seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either. A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely. But I still feel cheated," he said.
City were charged by the Premier League following an investigation into alleged breaches of regulations between 2009 and 2018.
The club were accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules.
They were also charged with failing to cooperate with an investigation.
City were referred to an independent commission and a hearing started behind closed doors in September 2024, lasting around 12 weeks.

In 2020, European football's governing body Uefa imposed a two-year European ban on City as well as a fine for breaking financial fair-play rules, though that ban was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
c00e3d040aa28112: KUALA LUMPUR: Former world No. 1 Datuk Nicol David has been a global ambassador and driving force in getting squash into the Olympics, and it was poetic justice that Malaysians Ng Eain Yow and S. Sivasangari became the sport's first qualifiers for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Eain Yow and Sivasangari did it in style by defending their men's and women's individual golds respectively at the Asian Games today, with eight-time world champion Nicol present at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena to cheer on the duo.
As the Asiad winners, Eain Yow and Sivasangari not only became the first two squash players to qualify for the 2028 Olympics, but also the first athletes from any sport to secure their places.

Nicol, who famously said she would love to trade her eight world titles for an Olympic gold medal, retired in 2019 without fulfilling that dream but had led global campaigns to get squash into the Olympics.
She succeeded when the International Olympic Committee gave the sport the nod in 2023.
Nicol was elated by the Malaysian duo's success.
"Malaysia has Olympians in squash for the first time in history. Congratulations to Sivasangari and Ng Eain Yow. So proud of you both," posted Nicol on Facebook.

Meanwhile, former Asian Games champion and Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia (SRAM) deputy president Azlan Iskandar, another player who retired without the chance to compete at the Olympics, hailed the duo's outstanding performances.

"Malaysia have met the Asian Games target, and as SRAM deputy president, I'm extremely proud of Eain Yow and Sivasangari. They played exceptionally well today," said Azlan, who won gold at the 2010 Guangzhou Games.
"Eain Yow was having a rough patch in recent times, but he turned it around in the final. He was simply excellent.
"They have also qualified for the Olympics, so big congratulations to them. They truly deserve to win and also earn their places at the Olympics."

Azlan, the deputy chef de mission, was also present to witness Malaysia's double-gold effort and is looking forward to the players pushing for another double in the men's and women's team events, which begin tomorrow.
389f089c8781a680: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen from Negeri Sembilan have arrived at Menara Dato Onn here for a meeting with BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on the constitutional crisis in the state.

0e78793025bf69d8: SEREMBAN: Police are investigating the possibility of bullying in connection with the death of a male Form Two student at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, including allegations that the victim was beaten after being suspected of vaping.

f9f8a4b595e1a65b: NAGOYA: For someone who looks up to Jamaican legend Usain Bolt as an inspiration, being crowned Asia's sprint king has not satisfied Thai sensation Puripol Boonson.

The 20-year-old sprinter is determined to continue breaking records and clocking faster times in the future to follow the footsteps of multiple Olympic champion Bolt — arguably the greatest sprinter the world has witnessed.
Bolt still holds the world records for the 100m at 9.58s and 200m at 19.19s, both set at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin, will be the benchmark as Puripol aims to go breaking records.
The Thai ace has created shockwaves at the ongoing Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games by winning gold in the 100m and 200m, while also setting new records in both events.
In the 100m, Puripol broke the Games record twice, starting with a time of 9.91 seconds in the semi-finals before lowering it to 9.90s in the final to claim the gold medal.
He won the 200m today, clocking 19.88 to equal the Asian record held by China's Xie Zhenye, set at the 2019 Diamond League in London.
However, the achievements have not made Puripol complacent, as he wants to continue pushing his limits in pursuit of even faster times.
"I may not be able to give an exact figure for the time I can achieve next, but I promise myself that I will become faster than I am now and break more records," Puripol said after the 200m final.
Puripol said the secret behind his continued improvement was consistent training and a strong determination to achieve his targets.
"Training... and having determination. I train hard, work hard and give everything," he added.
He added that mental strength was also an important element when dealing with pressure on a major stage such as the Asian Games, especially when competing with the target of winning gold.
"I don't think there was much difference before coming here and when competing. Maybe I was just more excited because we came with the desire to win medals," he said.
Puripol's rise to becoming Asia's fastest sprinter has progressed rapidly since he won three gold medals in the 100m, 200m and 4x100m during the 2021 SEA Games in Hanoi at the age of 16.
He then won silver in the 100m at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games behind Zhen Ye before adding another silver at the 2024 World Under-20 Championships in Lima, Peru.
Last year, Puripol made history as the first Southeast Asian sprinter to break the 10-second barrier when he clocked 9.94 at the 2025 SEA Games in Bangkok.
6124fc7187ebad54: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan digesa mewujudkan satu prosedur operasi standard (SOP) antibuli di peringkat nasional yang boleh diguna pakai merentas institusi pendidikan bagi memastikan setiap kes ditangani dengan cepat dan seragam.

Bekas timbalan menteri pendidikan P Kamalanathan berkata ketika ini Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM), Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan Kementerian Pertahanan mempunyai SOP masing-masing dalam menangani isu berkenaan.

Katanya, perlindungan terhadap pelajar tidak seharusnya berbeza hanya kerana mereka belajar di institusi bawah kementerian berlainan, termasuk sekolah berasrama penuh (SBP), Maktab Rendah Sains Mara (MRSM) atau Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM).

“Kita memerlukan satu SOP anti-buli nasional dengan garis masa yang jelas – 24 jam untuk memberi respons, tujuh hari untuk menjalankan siasatan dan 14 hari untuk mengambil tindakan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Gesaan berkenaan dibuat ketika isu keselamatan pelajar kembali mendapat perhatian susulan kematian seorang pelajar Tingkatan Dua di sebuah sekolah sukan di Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan.

Mengulas lanjut, Kamalanathan berkata usaha membanteras buli juga tidak boleh bergantung kepada hukuman semata-mata kerana pencegahan lebih penting untuk memastikan masalah dapat dikesan sebelum menjadi serius.
Beliau mencadangkan nisbah warden kepada pelajar di sekolah berasrama penuh dikaji semula, peranan kaunselor diperkasakan dan portal Aduan Buli dipastikan benar-benar sulit serta mesra kanak-kanak.
“Protokol pengesanan awal juga perlu diwujudkan supaya guru dapat mengenal pasti masalah sebelum buli berlaku.
“Guru dan kaunselor perlu menjadi tonggak utama dalam usaha pencegahan di sekolah,” katanya.

Kamalanathan turut menekankan kepentingan pendidikan komunikasi dan empati, termasuk mengajar pelajar cara menghormati orang lain, bertindak apabila menyaksikan kejadian buli serta mendapatkan bantuan apabila berdepan masalah.

Menurutnya, ibu bapa juga perlu memainkan peranan sebagai penjaga utama dengan memberi perhatian terhadap perubahan tingkah laku anak masing-masing dan membantu membendung gejala buli bermula dari rumah.

“Sekolah dan warga pendidik ada untuk memberi sokongan, tetapi ibu bapa juga perlu memainkan peranan mereka,” katanya yang menyokong Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek dan KPM dalam menangani kes buli.

1865af9a936bea66: MADRID: A growing protest camp in the heart of Madrid over unaffordable housing pushed Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez on Sunday to pledge swift government action.
Hundreds of protesters on the weekend set up tents in the capital's busy Puerta del Sol public square to press their demands.
The movement was triggered by a police eviction on Wednesday of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong Madrid apartment.
The woman, Maricarmen Abascal, was carried out on a stretcher after the police broke down her door, in a scene that caused widespread outrage.
Her plight tapped into long-simmering resentment in Spain's major cities over spiralling costs to rent or buy homes.
Tens of thousands of protesters took to Madrid's streets on Saturday, rattling keys and blowing whistles.
Authorities said 25,000 people took part, while the Madrid Tenants' Union, which organised the protest, said over 300,000 turned out.
Many then set up their tent camp in Puerta del Sol, vowing to stay until housing access is improved, or the government falls.

"We'll stay as long as necessary. Even as we mobilise the pressure keeps mounting, and we're already at our limits," one 28-year-old protester, who gave his first name as Sergio, said in front of his tent.
The housing problem in Spain has become a burning issue ahead of a general election due to take place next year.

Sanchez, in a political rally organised Sunday by his Socialist Party, addressed the evicted woman, saying: "Maricarmen, I have a message for you. The government is working all out to present the law on housing".
He urged other political parties to back the bill, which is expected to contain measures such as the automatic renewal of rental contracts and further restrictions on evictions.
However, Sanchez's party lacks a majority in Spain's parliament, where it is unclear whether the package would be approved. A similar bill was defeated earlier this year.
'Can't take any more'
The Madrid Tenants' Union urged on X for city residents to join the Puerta del Sol protest.
"We can't take any more. Either the rental system falls, or the government falls," it said.
Abascal was forced to leave the apartment where she had lived for 70 years after a real estate firm acquired the property and raised the rent by 275% to 2,650 (US$3,000), according to the union.
Now a symbol of Spain's housing crisis, she urged Spaniards to join the protest Saturday in a video message posted online just hours before it got under way.
"I want what has happened to me to serve so that it does not happen to other people," she said from hospital, where she has been treated for exhaustion since her eviction.
"I want it to encourage people to fight and to help change the laws that have allowed me to be evicted," she added in the video, posted by the tenants' union.
Many who took part in the street demonstration said that the rental market had become impossible.
A Madrid real-estate site, Idealista, estimates that rent has nearly doubled in the past decade.

"It is a struggle to find a place you can afford, then you live in fear of being forced out," demonstrator Enrique Ortega de Miguel, a 38-year-old graphic designer who lives with his mother, told AFP.

Puerta del Sol - a busy hub intensively used by commuters and tourists - has been the venue for past protests. In 2011, young demonstrators railing against poor economic conditions and corruption occupied it for three weeks.
The Bank of Spain estimates the country of around 50 million people is short of 700,000 homes, based on the gap between demand and new construction.
Spain has little public housing, while rents have been driven up by increased demand, including from tourism and population growth linked to immigration, analysts say.

137f58066b7c37ab: NAGOYA, Sept 27 — The Asian Games has crowned teenage champions before, but this edition has witnessed stunning successes by child prodigies, culminating in Yuki Kurihara standing atop the podium aged just 11.
The Japanese primary school student demolished opponents three times his age on the way to a historic gold in eSports in Aichi-Nagoya.
He is Japan’s youngest Asian Games champion in history and almost certainly the youngest the Games have ever seen.
Kurihara did not even react after winning Saturday’s final in Puyo Puyo Champions, a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.
The boy, who does not turn 12 until June and wants to be a train driver when he grows up, later explained that he felt “embarrassed”.
Kurihara’s face was splashed across national newspapers on Sunday.
There is no publicly available official list of the youngest medallists ever at the Games, which were first contested in 1951.
But the introduction in recent editions of events intended to attract younger viewers has resulted in some eye-catching displays by children.
In skateboarding, Taiwan’s 12-year-old Ku Yong-yan took home silver on Friday in the “men’s” park final.
The winner, Japan’s Izuru Nagahara, was a relative veteran at 15.
Nagahara had anaesthetic injections in his knee to dull the pain from injury before his winning run.
Also in the skateboarding was Mazel Paris of the Philippines, who was just nine when she competed at the previous Asian Games.
Asked what has changed since Hangzhou in 2023, the 12-year-old replied: “I got taller for sure.”
This week will see another teenage phenomenon enter the fray with India’s 15-year-old cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
Abuse concerns
But the presence of young children competing on the international stage against adults and under expectations to win for their country comes with a caveat.
Kanae Doi, Japan director at Human Rights Watch, said ahead of the Games that “moments of triumph do not come easily. They are built on years of disciplined training, often beginning in childhood”.
“At its best, that journey should provide children with the joy of play and competition, along with opportunities for physical, mental and personal growth,” she wrote in the Japan Times.
“Many young athletes instead encounter physical, verbal and even sexual abuse in the very environments meant to help them develop.”
She said that in Games host Japan, children “frequently experience abuse in sports training within Japanese schools, federations and elite sports programmes”.
In 2024, the International Olympic Committee released its consensus statement on youth athletes at the Olympic Games.
It noted that 50 per cent of common mental health conditions first emerge before 18.
Adolescent athletes are also more susceptible to certain injuries, it said.
Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi became the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze aged 12.
Now a teenager and hotly tipped to make a splash at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, Yu is one of the faces of the Nagoya Games with three golds, all in record times.
But when it came to reporters swarming around her after races, she looked all of her 13 years.
“Interviews are way harder than the race,” she said.
Under pressure
Each sport has its own rules on minimum age.
For World Aquatics, the minimum age for major international championships is 14 but exceptions can be made for younger swimmers if, like Yu, they are fast enough.
Yu has spoken previously about struggling to balance her swimming with school work.
Yu’s team-mate Zhang Yufei, 28, a multiple Olympic gold medallist and world champion, said the youngster’s stunning displays were no longer a shock.
But she cautioned: “I hope she can withstand that pressure.” — AFP
fac39fd1b33e6d86: AGLIANO TERME, Sept 27 — Wine growers in Italy’s Piedmont region are celebrating a bountiful harvest despite the extreme heat but warn they have to cut production because of trade headwinds and changing consumer habits.
In Agliano Terme, where vine-covered hills stretch as far as the eye can see, a dozen farm workers were picking the last Barbera grapes -- a variety behind one of the region’s most popular red wines.
“We started harvesting at the end of July, which is unheard of,” said Filippo Mobrici, 59, head of the Barbera d’Asti Consortium.
“But I’ve never seen such a beautiful vintage, both in terms of quantity and quality. It’s a five-star harvest,” the winemaker said.
The summer of 2026 was the hottest ever recorded in this northern Italian region between the Alps and the Po Valley, with an average temperature of 21.6°C and peaks of 40 near Agliano Terme.
But the winter had been rainy, and the beginning of spring as well.
“The vines were able to build up sufficient water reserves so that, despite the extreme heat of recent months, the grapes reached maturity in good conditions,” Mobrici said.
Winemakers also protected the grapes from the sun by keeping more foliage on than usual.

But, like many Italian regions, Piedmont has produced too much wine in recent years and growers are struggling to sell it in markets disrupted by wars, US tariffs, and younger generations which drink a bit less.
As a result, Barbera d’Asti producers have decided to limit volumes of the variety collected this year from nine tonnes to 8.5 tonnes per hectare.
‘Bold choices’
Producers are also putting less wine on the market.
Stocks in Italy, the world’s leading wine-producing country, were up 6.9 per cent year-on-year in July, according to official data.
The stored volume reached the equivalent of more than 5.6 billion bottles, nearly one year of production.
In Piedmont, some winegrowers have chosen to turn part of their production into vinegar this year.
Italy’s Wine Union (UIV) is calling for production to be planned according to the market and for no new vineyard plantings.
UIV president Lamberto Frescobaldi, a 33rd-generation Tuscan winegrower, said he was also open to the idea of removing old or unviable grapevines.
“It’s time to take responsibility for making bold choices, even unpopular ones,” he said earlier this year.
In Agliano Terme, Filippo Mobrici refuses to consider the idea of uprooting vines.
“For us, vineyards are not just a production tool,” he said.
“They are an expression of our culture and a key element in shaping and preserving the land. We do not want to uproot ourselves.”

A few kilometres further south, in San Marzano Oliveto, 41-year-old Luca Garberoglio is also pleased with a fine harvest and insists that stocks are “manageable” at the scale of the small Barbera d’Asti area.
Like many neighbouring producers, his family estate Carussin has succeeded in moving upmarket thanks to the production of organic wines exported in particular to Scandinavia.
And, because of climate change, the taste is changing.
Barbera d’Asti, “traditionally dominated by notes of cherry and plum, is increasingly evolving toward more concentrated aromas of blackberry and blackcurrant”, Garberoglio said after a tasting. — AFP
2c12558483e0a7fe: PHNOM PENH, Sept 27 — Interpol has flagged that online financial and romance fraud linked to organised syndicates is posing a growing threat to Asian economies, as Cambodia and Myanmar move to dismantle illicit scam operations.
Interpol’s Director of Taskforce Coordination Directorate, Nicholas Court, said millions of dollars are lost daily to fraud worldwide, and South-east Asia is no exception.

“We see a lot of different types of investment fraud, especially involving cryptocurrencies that is becoming more prevalent. Romance fraud has existed for decades but is becoming worse because of the use of social media and dating apps and people using the internet to find love and romance,” Court told Bernama.
He spoke on the sidelines of the International Conference on Combating Online Scams, which was held in Phnom Penh from September 23 to 24.

The second edition of Interpol’s Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment, released in March, estimated that financial fraud resulted in worldwide losses of about US$442 billion (RM1.8 trillion) last year alone.

What initially started as regional scam operations has transformed into global-level crime networks, with centres discovered across multiple regions hiring thousands of young people to perpetrate online fraud.

Well-financed criminal organisations have been using several South-east Asian countries, such as Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar, to launch their nefarious activities against vulnerable citizens across the globe.
“Every day, losses could be hundreds of thousands or even millions of euros at any point, and Asian businesses are definitely victims.

“So, it’s a really significant threat. A lot of countries see it as a national security threat even now because the amount of money that is leaving economies and countries and going into the pockets of criminals is vast.s
“People are committing suicide somewhere in the world every day as a result of being the victim of fraud, and businesses are closing down all the time,” he said.
Interpol’s Operation Haechi, conducted from April to August last year, uncovered US$342 million (RM1.4 billion) in illicit funds and blocked 68,000 bank accounts across 40 countries.

The operation targeted cyber-enabled financial crimes, including voice phishing, romance scams, online sextortion, investment fraud, money laundering linked to illegal online gambling, business email compromise and e-commerce fraud.

Romance fraud involves scammers establishing fake relationships with victims through social media, dating apps or messaging platforms before fleecing them of money by fabricating emergencies or financial problems. — Bernama
b7045a53a63e90d6: PENJWEN (Iraq), Sept 27 — Kurdistan resident Ahmed Faraj was just a child when his city became a battlefield in the Iran-Iraq conflict. Decades later, with the Middle East at war, he fears his home might be drawn in again.
For months, drones and missiles have buzzed over his lush green hometown of Penjwen bordering Iran, as the Islamic republic and the United States fight a war that has engulfed most of the region.

Iran and its allied Iraqi armed factions have intensified attacks on bases hosting US troops, as well as against Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, whose fighters have long sought refuge in Kurdistan’s mountains.
While the initial violence has largely subsided, Faraj worries that if fighting resumes, the conflict could escalate, putting his city at risk because “in war, borders no longer exist”.
“I clearly remember Penjwen’s destruction,” the 57-year-old told AFP as he sipped his tea at one of the city’s busiest markets.
Led by Saddam Hussein, Iraq attacked neighbouring Iran in September 1980, triggering an eight-year war that is estimated to have killed hundreds of thousands of people on both sides.
Faraj said one of his sharpest memories was from a year later, when Iran attacked his hometown, resulting in “dozens of civilian casualties”.

Eventually, once Penjwen was deserted, “the Iraqi regime demolished the town itself, flattening all the houses with TNT and bulldozers so that Iranian forces couldn’t enter and establish a base there”, he added.
Haunted by a memory
Between 1987 and 1988, Saddam’s government carried out the “Anfal Operation” that is thought to have killed around 180,000 Kurds.
Following a US-led invasion of Iraq, Saddam was toppled in 2003 and hanged three years later, putting an end to Iraqi proceedings against him on charges of genocide over the Anfal campaign.
Former parliamentarian Abdul Rahman Ali Reda was also a child when the war broke out, and one incident still haunts him: when Iraqi forces burned down his family home on a hill in Penjwen.
“That sight has never left me,” he said, now 53 years old.
“Homes, schools, government offices and religious sites were all levelled to the ground, and even after all these years, many houses remain in ruins and have never been rebuilt,” Reda told AFP.
He believes border-area residents suffer the most in wars, and these days they must always be prepared “for any potential disaster”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Hadi Abdullah, a 56-year-old Iraqi Kurd, speaks with an AFP journalist in the Penjwen district, near the border with Iran in Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region September 21, 2026. — AFP pic
Iraqi Kurdistan is home to thousands of Iranian Kurds opposed to the Islamic republic, including militant groups that have long had bases there.
These groups have also maintained a clandestine presence in Kurdish-majority western Iran.
Among them is the Komala party, founded in 1969 by students and intellectuals in Tehran and Kurdish cities. Iranian drones and missiles have repeatedly hit its fighters in the ongoing war.
‘Not our war’
Party member Idriss Kolahduzi told AFP that Tehran has dispatched reinforcements to predominantly Kurdish regions in Iran, including the border with Iraqi Kurdistan, in recent months.
“Kurds don’t have factories or plants, they rely mostly on agriculture in border regions,” he said, warning that additional military deployment would only “burden” them.
Kolahduzi said he believes “Iran fears a potential uprising” in Kurdish areas.
At the start of the Middle East war, media reports suggested that Iranian Kurdish groups might collaborate with the United States.
Several of the groups, however, said they were waiting for an uprising in Iran before they would cross the border and attempt to overthrow the government.
Tehran threatened to target “all facilities” in Iraqi Kurdistan if militants crossed into Iran.
Penjwen resident Omid Hassan told AFP that “the sound of any plane or missile overhead brings back the times when the city was a front-line battlefield in the Iran-Iraq war”.
It “fills me with worry and sorrow”, the 57-year-old said.
At a local cafe, Hadi Abdullah, a civil servant wearing traditional Kurdish shalwar, said his greatest concern was the economic fallout from the war, as prices climb and the Iraqi dinar fluctuates.
“This is not our war, and we should not be dragged into it,” the 56-year-old told AFP. — AFP
bd0a152a9eb24e67: GENEVA, Sept 27 — The Swiss are voting today on a much-debated proposal to tighten their country’s cherished neutrality, with polls indicating most will reject the initiative championed by the hard-right and dubbed “pro-Russian” by opponents.
In-person voting on those and other topics will begin at 10am (0800 GMT) as part of Switzerland’s direct democracy system, although most people vote in advance by post.
The Swiss widely embrace their neutrality, but an initiative to enshrine a strict definition into the constitution has exposed deep disagreement over what that neutrality entails.
Switzerland’s traditional position is one of well-armed military neutrality, but Russia’s war in Ukraine reopened questions over its non-engagement in foreign conflicts.

Concerned over Bern’s decision to back the European Union’s economic pressure, the pro-sovereignty Pro Switzerland organisation collected enough signatures to trigger a public vote under the country’s direct democracy system on better anchoring neutrality in its constitution.
The proposal has been roundly rejected by nearly the entire political establishment, with opinion polls indicating most voters will do the same.
Moscow, which has slammed Switzerland for joining the EU sanctions and accused Bern of abandoning its neutrality, has meanwhile praised the initiative — dubbed “pro-Russian” by some opponents.
The proposal calls for the constitution to guarantee that Swiss neutrality is “armed and perpetual”.

It would prevent Switzerland, whose neutrality dates back to 1516 and has been internationally recognised since 1815, from establishing closer ties with Nato and would rule out any military alliance except if the country were attacked.
And it would prohibit imposing sanctions unless called for by the United Nations.
‘Perpetual armed neutrality’
All sides in the debate argue that they want to maintain Switzerland’s neutrality.
Both the Swiss government and parliament have rejected the proposal, arguing it is too dogmatic and would limit the country’s room for manoeuvre at a time of soaring geopolitical tensions.
“Neutrality has always been applied with a degree of flexibility,” Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis insisted during a recent televised debate.
While Switzerland had no plans to lift a ban on selling arms to countries in conflict, including Ukraine, he stressed that “neutrality does not mean indifference”.
The country, he said, would “not look away when we see violations of the very international rules that allow us to live in peace”.
Nearly all major political parties have also turned their nose up at the initiative, with the exception of the hard-right Swiss People’s Party (SVP) — Switzerland’s largest.
“Our goal is to foster peace, diplomacy and dialogue,” SVP vice president Celine Amaudruz said during a televised debate.
“To achieve that, we must maintain credibility through perpetual armed neutrality,” she insisted.
While initial opinion polls had indicated that the vote might be tight, the final two surveys suggested a clear majority of voters — well above 60 per cent — would reject the initiative.

Polls also suggested voters would reject the other national initiative on today’s ballot, put forward by a non-partisan citizen’s movement and calling for the country to raise its food self-sufficiency rate to 70 per cent, up from 42 per cent in 2024.
The government has warned that target would be difficult if not impossible to reach, while most major parties also rejecting it as unrealistic. — AFP
3301993b808d0396: PETALING JAYA: A former deputy education minister has called for a "uniformed SOP" to deal with bullying in schools and higher learning institutions following the recent death of a Form 2 student.
P Kamalanathan said the education, higher education, and defence ministries have different SOPs at the moment.
“We need one national anti-bullying SOP with a clear timeline: 24 hours to respond, seven days to investigate, 14 days to action," he said in a statement.
Kamalanathan, who held the post from 2013 to 2018, said there is a need to focus on teaching children how to communicate, and instill empathy.
He said that based on his research, many children lack emotional literacy.
“We teach them STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics), but we must also teach them how to communicate respect, how to be an active bystander, and how to seek help,” he said.
He said there was also a need to review the warden-to-student ratio in fully residential schools, empower counsellors, and make the portal to report bullying truly anonymous and child-friendly.
Last year, it was reported that three wardens were assigned to every 50 hostel students.
“Early detection protocols should be put in place where teachers can identify the issue before the bullying starts. Teachers and counsellors should be the backbone of prevention in schools,” he said.
His proposals come in the wake of a student's death at a sports school in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, on Friday.
Idlan Fareeq Shahril, 14, was found unconscious in the school dormitory before being rushed to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Police, who have detained a student, are investigating the case for murder, with Idlan’s family claiming that he was bullied.
Kamalanathan also called on parents to play their roles as primary caregivers, telling them to pay attention to their children's behaviour, and help root out bullying at home.
“The school and its staff are here to support, but parents need to do their part, too,” he said.
